body.p: The plugin ships with five themesbuilt-inbuilt-in themes, each designed for a specific publishing context. Set the theme with the epub.theme parameter:

row.entry: Neutral palette, balanced typography, suitable for most content types
Serif fonts, conservative muted palette, tight spacing, footnote and bibliography emphasis, minimal decorative elements
Elegant serif body text (Georgia stack), generous margins, refined chapter headings, warm accent colors, optimized for long-form reading with drop cap support
Software documentation, API references, technical guides
Code block emphasis with enhanced syntax highlighting colors, monospace prominence, compact tables, cool blue accent palette, optimized for code-heavy content
Clear visual hierarchy, callout styling, exercise and activity boxes, highlighted key terms, step-by-step formatting with numbered procedures

body.p: Theme names are case-insensitive parameterscase-insensitive: Fiction, FICTION, and fiction all resolve to the same stylesheet. The plugin normalizes the value internally before matching.
body.note: If no theme is specified or the theme name does not match a built-in theme, only the base epub-default.css is applied. No error is raised — the plugin simply skips the theme stylesheet.
